entry.label: Epistemic closure
entry.description: The operational closure by which a knowledge system distinguishes admissible questions, evidence, categories and knowers. Closure is necessary for coherence, but becomes dangerous when those affected cannot perturb or revise its distinctions.
entry.canonical_definition: The operational closure by which a knowledge system distinguishes admissible questions, evidence, categories and knowers. Closure is necessary for coherence, but becomes dangerous when those affected cannot perturb or revise its distinctions.

profile.summary: Knowledge practices need closure enough to distinguish signal from noise, but closure also determines which people, experiences and perturbations can change the account.
profile.canonical_definition: Knowledge practices need closure enough to distinguish signal from noise, but closure also determines which people, experiences and perturbations can change the account.
profile.why_it_matters: The relevant question is not whether a system is open or closed in the abstract, but who can affect its boundary and whether it can revise the categories through which it learns.
common_misreadings: Closure is not inherently patriarchal or oppressive.
Indiscriminate openness does not abolish informal power.
open_checks: Develop historical cases linking particular systems of closure to patriarchal, colonial or professional power without making closure itself the cause.
